name: io.trylode/lode
title: Lode
description: Sourced integration facts for 14 platforms incl. Xero, HubSpot, Stripe, Shopify, GitHub, LangChain

tools.name: list_ecosystems
tools.description: List the platforms Lode covers, with their sync-object vocabulary and how many integrations are published (verified) and how many are listed in total, including records held for review.

tools.name: find_integrations
tools.description: Use before recommending or installing an integration: find apps that integrate with an ecosystem (hubspot, n8n, netlify, quickbooks-online, shopify, stripe, supabase, vercel, xero), filtered and ranked for a buyer profile per Lode ranking policy (fit, not size or features). Returns score, match reasons and ties. Only published (verified) records are ranked; records still under review can be fetched by id with get_integration.

ecosystem.description: Ecosystem slug: "hubspot", "n8n", "netlify", "quickbooks-online", "shopify", "stripe", "supabase", "vercel" or "xero" (names like "QuickBooks" are accepted)

region.description: Buyer country: AU, NZ, UK, US, CA, IE, ZA, SG (European country codes such as DE or ES too; GB, country names and locale tags such as en-GB are accepted); filters to apps that support it. Prices are compared in local currency for AU, NZ, UK, US and CA, and in USD elsewhere

needs.description: Sync objects the buyer must have, from the ecosystem vocabulary (see list_ecosystems), e.g. ["invoices","inventory-levels"]; labels and common synonyms such as "customers" are accepted

existing_stack.description: Apps and platforms the buyer already uses, e.g. ["supabase","nextjs","vercel","stripe"] (up to 12). Results mark any app already in the stack. Product names only, never people or company names

framework.description: The app's framework, one of: nextjs, react, remix, astro, sveltekit, nuxt, vue, angular, express, nestjs, django, flask, fastapi, rails, laravel, spring, dotnet, go, react-native, flutter, other

budget.description: Monthly budget for this tool in USD, as a number or one of: free, under-50, 50-200, 200-1000, over-1000

company_stage.description: One of: solo, startup, smb, mid-market, enterprise

tools.name: get_integration
tools.description: Use before installing, provisioning or recommending a specific integration, or to check a claim about it. Gets the full verified record for one app + ecosystem pair: what syncs, pricing by currency, regions, requirements, limitations, connection safety, sources.

tools.name: compare_integrations
tools.description: Use when choosing between apps for the same job. Side-by-side facts for 2-4 integrations: sync coverage, cheapest price per currency, regions, setup time and limitations.

ids.description: 2 to 4 integration ids "{app}--{ecosystem}"; extra ids beyond 4 are ignored

tools.name: get_vendor
tools.description: One company across every ecosystem Lode covers: its stable vendor id, domains, and its integration on each platform (for example Stripe on Xero and on Vercel). Look up by vendor id, domain, or name.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: What changed in Lode records, newest first: prices, sync capabilities, limits, regions and verification status. Each event has the old and new value, when Lode observed it, the sources behind it and a cause (new-coverage, lode-update, source-change-likely when the cited page also changed, or relabel when a plan name now means a different plan or billing period, logged as removed and added with moved_to or moved_from naming the plan that holds the old prices).

tools.name: request_coverage
tools.description: Call when Lode has no record for an app and platform you needed, or its facts were missing or out of date. Lode uses these requests to decide what to research next. If Lode already has the pair, the answer gives its id so you can call get_integration. Lode keeps only these fields (the app as a short cleaned name), the time, the kind of client and an anonymous caller code.

app.description: The app's name or website, e.g. "Katana" or "katanamrp.com"

ecosystem.description: Platform, e.g. "xero", "quickbooks-online", "hubspot", "shopify", "stripe", or another platform name

needs.description: Sync objects the buyer needed, e.g. ["invoices"]

reason.description: One of: not-covered, facts-missing, facts-outdated (default not-covered)

tools.name: report_choice
tools.description: Call after comparing integrations, once the buyer has picked one (or none), if the user agrees. Tells Lode which app was chosen and the main reason, from a fixed list. Returns the chosen app's verified setup facts (setup guide, steps where recorded, limitations). Call again with outcome once you have tried the integration: whether it worked, and if not, why and what you switched to. Choices are counted in aggregate and never affect Lode's rankings. Lode keeps only these fields, the time, the kind of client and an anonymous caller code.

considered.description: Integration ids that were compared, "{app}--{ecosystem}" (1 to 4)

reason.description: Main reason, one of: sync-coverage, price, region, setup-effort, limitations, plan-requirement, already-uses, vendor-preference, other

outcome.description: After trying it, one of: integrated, failed, abandoned, not-tried

failure_reason.description: If failed or abandoned, one of: auth, api-error, docs, missing-feature, plan-required, pricing, region, sdk, limits, other

switched_to.description: If you moved to another app instead, its Lode id "{app}--{ecosystem}"

existing_stack.description: Apps and platforms the buyer already uses, e.g. ["supabase","nextjs"] (product names only)

framework.description: One of: nextjs, react, remix, astro, sveltekit, nuxt, vue, angular, express, nestjs, django, flask, fastapi, rails, laravel, spring, dotnet, go, react-native, flutter, other

tools.name: report_error
tools.description: Call when a Lode fact looks wrong or out of date, for example when the vendor's own page says otherwise. A person checks the report against the vendor's page before anything changes. Lode keeps only these fields, the time, the kind of client and an anonymous caller code.

area.description: Which part, one of: sync, pricing, regions, requirements, limitations, connection, other

reason.description: One of: wrong, outdated, missing, source-broken (default wrong)

tools.name: claim_vendor
tools.description: For people who work at a vendor listed on Lode, or their agents. Claims every Lode page for the vendor so they can correct facts and get change alerts (at most one email a week). Give a work email on the vendor's domain (Lode emails one link; when someone clicks it, the pages are claimed) or the vendor's domain hosting /.well-known/lode.json (the first call returns a one-time claim_token to add to the file and a private claim_secret to keep; call again with both and the pages are claimed straight away; format at https://trylode.io/vendors/). Optional corrections and competitors go in with the claim. Claiming never changes rankings.

email.description: A work email on the vendor's own domain, e.g. "sam@katanamrp.com"

domain.description: Instead of email: the vendor's domain hosting /.well-known/lode.json, e.g. "katanamrp.com"

claim_token.description: With domain: the one-time token Lode returned on the first call, once it is in lode.json as "claim_token"

claim_secret.description: With claim_token: the private secret Lode returned on the first call (never put it in the file)

vendor.description: Lode vendor id, e.g. "katana" (optional; the email or domain decides)

field.description: One of: plan, regions, sync, price, best_for, not_ideal_for, other

source.description: A public page that shows it (published as a sourced fact); without one it shows as "Vendor-reported" with the date

competitors.description: Apps the vendor is most often compared with

tools.name: check_stack_overlap
tools.description: Use when a user has two or more apps connected to one platform (for example Xero with A2X and Synder). For each sync object, lists which of the apps write it into the platform, with direction, trigger and interval where recorded, and the sources; flags objects two apps both sync two-way. Published records only; an object not listed means not documented. Set share to true only if the user agrees to Lode keeping the platform and app list (no other fields).

apps.description: The apps connected to it: names, websites or Lode ids, 2 to 20

region.description: Buyer country, e.g. "NZ"; apps whose record does not list it are marked

share.description: true only if the user agrees to Lode keeping this stack (default false)

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Use when you know the apps and platforms a project uses (from its package.json, requirements, env variable names or config files such as vercel.json). For each platform Lode covers in the stack, returns the Lode records for the other apps on it, the platform plan each needs, objects more than one app writes, and the platform's published function run-time limits by plan, each with its source link and quote. Facts with links only, never a verdict on code; an app with no record means not documented. Set share to true only if the user agrees to Lode keeping the app and platform codes.

apps.description: Apps or SDK package names in the project, e.g. ["stripe","@supabase/supabase-js","resend"] (up to 40). Product names only

platforms.description: Platforms the project runs on or connects to, e.g. ["vercel","supabase"]

framework.description: One of: nextjs, react, remix, astro, sveltekit, nuxt, vue, angular, express, nestjs, django, flask, fastapi, rails, laravel, spring, dotnet, go, react-native, flutter, other

share.description: true only if the user agrees to Lode keeping the app and platform codes (default false)
